title: Counterfactual Auditing of Bias in Open-Source Large Language Models for Clinical Triage

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual single-variable injection of different race and ethnicity identifiers (e.g., White, Non-Hispanic Black, Hispanic, Asian) into clinical vignettes to measure shifts in Emergency Severity Index (ESI) predictions.
Counterfactual injection of primary language and interpreter needs into clinical triage prompts to evaluate undertriage and overtriage shifts in predicted clinical acuity.
Adding socioeconomic variables such as insurance status, neighborhood income level, area deprivation, and housing stability to clinical vignettes to evaluate changes in model triage behavior.
Evaluating ESI prediction shifts by injecting non-clinical patient context regarding primary care access, prior ED utilization, and recent hospitalization history.
Testing the sensitivity of triage predictions by inserting patient history elements like psychiatric diagnoses, substance use disorders, and health literacy into the prompt.
Injecting system and environmental factors such as arrival mode, ED crowding, arrival time, and urban/rural location into clinical vignettes to measure non-clinical influences on triage scores.
